hypothesis: Explicit prefetch or a different store policy may hide latency in the four-stream in-place transform and eight-stream IFFT-accumulate AVX2 GF8 loops.

analysis.in_place_transform_stores: Every stage is read by a later transform stage, so non-temporal stores would force immediate refetch and are not eligible.
analysis.final_stores: Final in-place butterflies are read-modify-write operations, so the destination line is already resident. Public outputs may be unaligned and may be consumed immediately; streaming stores would add an alignment path and an sfence without avoiding the load.
analysis.out_of_place_stores: The same backend callbacks also execute non-final stages and carry no final-stage contract, so silently applying streaming stores is unsafe as a general memory policy.
analysis.alignment: Public shards explicitly support unaligned pointers. Zen 5 has no aligned-instruction advantage for the already non-crossing aligned cases, while runtime alignment branches would remain in every hot callback.
analysis.restrict: The loops use explicit intrinsic loads and stores, so restrict does not remove alias checks or change the generated vector sequence; callback alias contracts also cannot be strengthened locally.
analysis.prefetch_scope: Measured T0 read hints and PREFETCHW output hints at 256, 512, and 1024 byte lead distances, issued once per 64-byte cache line with all hinted addresses kept inside their shard objects.

screen.result: No candidate had a credible 5 percent whole-codec gain. Several variants regressed the T=16 4 KiB encode by 6 to 9 percent; range or combined variants also produced reproducible neighboring losses above 2 percent.

notable_initial_hint.reason_for_followup: This was the only preliminary median at the promotion boundary, but the same candidate regressed T=64/K=192/1MiB to 0.9636124593444677 and T=128/K=128/64KiB to 0.9542876793945343.

conclusion: Zen 5 hardware prefetch plus the retained cache-resident payload tiling already covers these regular streams. Explicit hints add branch, prefetch, and code-footprint cost; no tested policy meets promotion criteria. Keep the production kernels unchanged.
